content.text: You don't need a buggy to enjoy golf in the Algarve. Several courses have flat or gently rolling ground that suits walkers, and a handful of short 9-hole courses are an easy way to play on foot.

This isn't a complete list. We've only included courses where we found enough information from the club or an independent golf guide, so a course that isn't mentioned here may still be a good walk. Terrain is also a matter of opinion: what feels easy to one golfer can feel tiring to another. **Last checked: November 2026.**
Flat Algarve golf courses that are easy to walk

**[Salgados](/courses/salgados)** has the strongest evidence of any course we checked. The club describes it as set on the flatlands behind Praia de Galé, Where2Golf says players generally walk it, and Teetimes.pt calls it totally flat, with a buggy optional. Flat doesn't mean easy, though: there's plenty of water, and the site is exposed to the wind.

**[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship)** is listed by Teetimes.pt as flat, with some gentle slopes on the approaches to the greens. Golfbreaks also describes its relatively flat appearance as deceptive, because of the streams and water hazards. The club itself mentions subtle slopes and raised greens.
**[Quinta do Lago Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal)** is described by Teetimes.pt as flat, with no severe slopes, and easy to walk. It's exposed, so expect to feel any breeze.
**[Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium)** is listed by Teetimes.pt as flat with minor slopes.

**[Amendoeira O'Connor](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor)** stays down in the valley on flat terrain among orange groves, according to Teetimes.pt, which contrasts it with the Faldo course on the hillside. The online green fee includes a buggy, if one is available, so walking won't save you money here.
Gently rolling courses near Tavira
**[Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria)** spans what the club calls gently sloping terrain leading towards the Ria Formosa. Teetimes.pt describes long rolling slopes and a fairly flat course.
**[Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima)**, its neighbour, has gentle, long rolling fairways with few major inclines, according to Teetimes.pt.
Short 9-hole courses for an easy round on foot
If you'd rather not walk 18 holes, a 9-hole course is the simplest answer.
**[Penina Resort Course](/courses/penina-resort)** is listed by Teetimes.pt as flat and easy walking. At 2,987 metres from the white tees, it's still a proper 9-hole course.

**[Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs)** is described by Teetimes.pt as flat with slight rolling slopes. Its price list has manual and electric trolleys but no buggies, so check with the course first if you might need to ride.
**[Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho)** is the shortest course we track, at 926 metres. The club doesn't have buggies to hire, but it does offer trolleys. Rental equipment is available until 3pm.
**[Balaia](/courses/balaia)** is a short par-3 course with a pull trolley on its price list, though Teetimes.pt notes it's hilly for a par 3.
More Algarve courses where a buggy may be optional
On these courses, the sources we checked don't treat a buggy as a must, so they may suit fit walkers, although most have some slopes:

[Espiche](/courses/espiche)'s own website calls it enjoyable to walk, while also mentioning elevation changes. Golfbreaks describes [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) as a flatter, links-style layout.

Teetimes.pt lists a buggy as optional at [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) and [Vilamoura Pinhal](/courses/vilamoura-pinhal), and as needed only if essential at [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf), the [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Pinheiros Altos](/courses/pinheiros-altos). At Pinheiros Altos, the same guide says the Olives nine is flat, while the Pines and Corks nines are more undulating.
Courses where you may want a buggy

Some golfers walk these too, but the sources we checked point towards riding. [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) says its course runs over hills and lists a buggy as recommended. Teetimes.pt calls a buggy essential at [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim), [Boavista](/courses/boavista), [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale), [Quinta do Lago North](/courses/quinta-do-lago-north) and [Vale do Lobo Ocean](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean). It also recommends one at [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal), [Benamor](/courses/benamor), [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos).

For prices and rules, see our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve). It also covers courses where a buggy comes with the green fee. You can also read more about [hilly golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/hilly-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).

content.text: Before you walk an Algarve golf course
**Check that walking is allowed.** Golfbreaks notes that walking policies vary by course, so ask when you book, especially if the green fee includes a buggy.
**Choose your tee time for the season.** In summer, an early start avoids the worst of the heat. Take plenty of water too, as the [Algarve golf in July](/guide/algarve-golf-in-july) guide explains.
**Reserve your trolley.** Rentals can be limited, and Balaia says its equipment is allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
